title.narrative: Sustainable Energy from BIOgas in Solomon Islands

description.narrative: Solomon Islands’ piggery sector faces an interconnected energy, environmental, and development challenge. Rural households and commercial piggeries rely on costly imported diesel and traditional firewood for energy while unmanaged organic wastes (notably pig slurry and municipal organics) pollute water and contribute to methane emissions, pressuring mangroves and coastal ecosystems and imposing health and time burdens on women and children. The versatility, sustainability, and waste-to-energy aspects of biogas technology make it a compelling solution for promoting energy efficiency and addressing environmental concerns faces by the country. However, this technology holds some barriers. Most smallholders and farms lack access to affordable finance for clean energy, have limited technical capacity to design and operate digesters, and operate without standards, service networks, or reliable after-sales support, constraints that further reinforce gender inequalities limiting women’s access to energy assets, decision making and technical roles. This 30-month SENBIOSIS project tackles these barriers by designing and piloting financial solutions for the manufacturing, deployment and successful management of biogas investments in the Solomon Islands, actively proposing women’s participation and decision-making roles. The project combines the establishment of a Biogas Lending Facility Mechanism that blends a revolving lending portfolio (with a first-loss guarantee) for household-scale and farm-scale digesters with targeted technical assistance, demonstration plants, and support policy reform. Activities cover beneficiary enrolment and resource mapping; biogas technology design and procurement; establishment of a dedicated Biogas Lending Facility with concessional terms; support the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock in establishing a local biogas manufacturer, construction of six demonstration systems (five household units and one commercial piggery system);

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
